steps.description: Implement a bootstrap experiment to measure N_c(w) (minimum hidden-layer width for zero-violation generalization) vs. constraint sample count w. First construct a simple linear constraint (rigid, low-dimensional) where zero violation is easily achievable, verify it works with a wide network (anchor point), then scan widths across multiple seeds and report N_c(w) trends. This is a pure ML/math problem — no physical system analogies.

plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The solution space bifurcates at critical sample width $w^*$ such that $N_c(w)$ exhibits a non-monotonic transition: initially flat for $w < w^*$ (rigid subspace), then increasing for $w > w^*$ as constraints intersect to form a disconnected manifold of isolated solutions, requiring wider networks to navigate topological barriers. | pro: This aligns with the "piecewise-linear topology" hint in git history and explains why bootstrap experiments might fail—local minima trap optimization when topology shifts. It is testable via loss landscape visualization and critical exponent analysis. | con: Requires high-resolution sampling near $w^*$; if the bifurcation is too sharp or the manifold curvature is high, standard L-BFGS may miss the transition, leading to false flat/increasing readings.

steps.description: The previous prediction (rigid subspace → flat/decreasing N_c(w)) was contradicted by the hypothesis (bifurcation → non-monotonic transition) and the surprise metric (1.0). This indicates a need to re-evaluate the constraint construction and verify if the solution space indeed transitions from rigid to disconnected manifold. I will design a numerical experiment to: (1) construct a low-dimensional linear constraint family (rigid case) and a higher-dimensional non-linear constraint family (flexible case), (2) train small feedforward networks using scipy.optimize.minimize(method='L-BFGS-B') to find the minimum width N_c(w) for zero violation (max abs error ≤ 1e-3 on held-out constraints), (3) perform width scans with multiple random seeds to ensure robustness, (4) analyze the trend of N_c(w) vs w to test the bifurcation hypothesis. This approach follows the "exploration" mode to search the design space for optimal parameters and validate the hypothesis through empirical evidence.
